================================================================================
STANDARD-LINUX TRACE
tkinter example.py: process start -> window.mainloop() begins
================================================================================
WHAT THIS IS
  A canonical, known-correct record of what a Tk/Tkinter application does on a
  standard Linux system up to the moment mainloop() begins, captured so it can
  be compared 1:1 against the same run inside the CheerpX VM (planned). Both a
  syscall trace and a per-call X11 (Xlib) function trace with arguments are
  included, cut at an identical marker so the two can be cross-correlated and
  later diffed against the CheerpX capture.

APP
  python-tkinter/example.py:
      import sys, tkinter as tk
      window = tk.Tk()
      greeting = tk.Label(text="I am working!")
      greeting.pack()
      window.update()
      print("TRACE_MAINLOOP_BEGIN", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)   # marker
      with open("/tmp/TRACE_MAINLOOP_BEGIN","w") as m: m.write("x") # marker
      window.mainloop()
  The marker is emitted immediately BEFORE window.mainloop(). Both sections
  below are cut after the marker, so everything shown happens strictly before
  the mainloop begins (Tk() construction, Label + pack, update()).

ENVIRONMENT
  guest userland : Alpine Linux 3.17.10, i686 (ELF32/i386), musl libc
  python3        : 3.10.15-r0
  python3-tkinter: 3.10.11-r0  (Tk 8.6.12-r1 / Tcl 8.6.12-r1)
  xvfb (X srvr)  : 21.1.8-r0  (:99, screen 1344x900x24, -nolisten tcp -ac)
  fontconfig     : 2.14.1-r0   freetype 2.12.1-r0
  libx11 1.8.7-r0  libxft 2.3.7-r0  libdrm 2.4.114-r0
  X default font : "fixed" (Tk uses CORE fonts; Xft is loaded but not used)
  execution      : the i386 userland is run under qemu-i386 user-mode
                   7.2.22 (linux-user) inside a Docker Desktop arm64 Linux VM
                   (guest uname: Linux 6.12.76-linuxkit ... i686). This is the
                   same Alpine 3.17 i386 userland the CheerpX guest runs, in a
                   deterministic emulated environment.
  X server       : Xvfb (same xorg-server 21.1.8 build as the guest's Xorg)

CAPTURE METHODS
  syscall trace  : qemu-i386 -strace (qemu user-mode built-in syscall tracer),
                   one line per syscall: "<pid> <name>(<args>) = <ret>".
                   NO per-syscall timestamps (qemu -strace limitation); the
                   X11-call trace carries timestamps and is the ordering
                   reference. Paths are guest paths; some syscalls (statx,
                   AF_UNIX sockets) are NOT path-translated by qemu-user.
  X11 call trace : LD_PRELOAD shim (python-tkinter/xcall-logger.c) interposing
                   libX11 entry points; each line:
                       X11<TAB><entry_ts_sec.usec><TAB><func>(<args>) -> <ret>
                   ts = CLOCK_MONOTONIC at function ENTRY. The section below is
                   sorted by entry timestamp so lines are in true call order.
                   Both direct app calls AND libX11-internal calls are captured
                   (Alpine's libX11 is not built with -Bsymbolic).
  cut point      : both sections cut AFTER the TRACE_MAINLOOP_BEGIN marker
                   (syscalls: the write(2) + open("/tmp/TRACE_MAINLOOP_BEGIN")
                   ; X11: the marker line in the logger's stderr stream).

================================================================================
SECTION 1: SYSCALL TRACE (up to mainloop begin)
  11911 syscalls. Notable: python interpreter startup (loader, lib
  loading, brk/mmap), locale/fontconfig init (incl. the per-file macOS
  metadata probes in /usr/share/fonts/encodings), the AF_UNIX connect to the X
  server (first compact sockaddr refused, retry with full sockaddr succeeds),
  X socket set to non-blocking, then the Xlib/Tk request/reply traffic.
================================================================================
